title: Alternative Text for Images
whyItMatters: When an image conveys meaning, users who cannot see it rely on text alternatives. Without this text, critical visual information is completely lost to screen readers.
learningObjectives: Understand the purpose of alternative text for images.
Identify when an image needs description versus when it is purely decorative.
Recognize the prevalence of missing alt text across the web.
lessonParagraphs: Images are a core part of digital design. However, an image is invisible to a screen reader unless it has alternative text. Alternative text, or alt text, is a hidden description that assistive technologies read aloud. When a meaningful image lacks this description, a person relying on a screen reader misses the information completely. According to the 2026 WebAIM Million report, missing alt text is the second most common accessibility failure on the internet, affecting 53.1 percent of homepages.

The first step in writing alt text is deciding if the image needs it at all. If an image is purely decorative and does not add meaning to the page, it can be marked as decorative so screen readers skip it. If the image carries meaning, such as a chart showing sales data or an icon indicating a successful submission, it requires clear and concise alt text. The description should focus on the exact meaning the image conveys rather than describing every visual detail.

Avene flags missing alternative text, helping designers catch this common issue. Understanding alt text is essential for holistic design. Providing a text alternative ensures that the core message of a layout reaches everyone, regardless of how they access the content.
keyTakeaways: Alternative text allows screen readers to describe images to users.
The 2026 WebAIM Million report found missing alt text on 53.1 percent of web homepages.
Decorative images can be skipped, but meaningful images require concise descriptions.
